columns.rationale: year has null_rate 0.0 and a single distinct_value of 2013.0, so it is cast from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER with no nullability concern.
month has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_values 1.0 through 6.0, all integral, so it is cast to INTEGER.
day has null_rate 0.0, min 1.0 and max 31.0 with integral sample_values (1.0-10.0), so it is cast to INTEGER.

dep_time has null_rate 0.029388 (4883 of 166158 nulls); per operator context a flight that never departed has no departure time, so nulls are retained; sample_values 1.0-10.0 are integral so it is cast to INTEGER and spelled out to departure_time.
dep_time null_count 4883 (null_rate 0.029388) corresponds to flights that never departed per operator context, so a boolean is_cancelled flag is derived as true when dep_time is null.
sched_dep_time has null_rate 0.0 and integral sample_values from 500.0 to 530.0, so it is cast to INTEGER and spelled out to scheduled_departure_time.

dep_delay has null_rate 0.029388 matching dep_time's null pattern (cancelled flights); sample_values -33.0 to -19.0 are integral minutes, so it is cast to INTEGER, suffixed with its unit per naming convention, and retained nullable.

arr_time has null_rate 0.0307 (5101 nulls), slightly higher than dep_time, consistent with flights that departed but lack a recorded arrival; integral sample_values support casting to INTEGER and retaining nulls.
sched_arr_time has null_rate 0.0 with integral sample_values 1.0-10.0, so it is cast to INTEGER and spelled out to scheduled_arrival_time.
arr_delay has null_rate 0.032981 (5480 nulls) aligned with missing arrival data; integral sample_values -86.0 to -67.0 support INTEGER, suffixed with its unit, and retained nullable.
carrier has null_rate 0.0 and 16 distinct two-letter values (9E, AA, AS, ...); it is a code column so renamed to carrier_code per naming convention.
flight has null_rate 0.0, integral sample_values 1.0-10.0 and max 8500.0, so it is cast to INTEGER and renamed to flight_number.
tailnum has null_rate 0.009154 (1521 nulls) with no stated cause, so it is retained nullable; it is an abbreviated name per operator context so spelled out to tail_number.
origin has null_rate 0.0 and exactly 3 distinct_values (EWR, JFK, LGA); it is an airport code so renamed to origin_code.
dest has null_rate 0.0 and 100 distinct airport codes (sample ABQ, ACK, ALB...); it is an airport code so renamed to dest_code.

air_time has null_rate 0.032981 (5480 nulls) matching flights with no recorded arrival; integral sample_values 20.0-29.0 support INTEGER, and the measure is suffixed with its unit per naming convention.
distance has null_rate 0.0 and integral sample_values from 80.0 to 185.0 with max 4983.0, so it is cast to INTEGER and suffixed with its unit, distance_miles.
hour has null_rate 0.0 and 19 distinct integral values from 5.0 to 23.0, so it is cast to INTEGER.
minute has null_rate 0.0 and integral sample_values 0.0-9.0 with max 59.0, so it is cast to INTEGER.

time_hour has null_rate 0.0 and ISO8601 sample_values like 2013-01-01T10:00:00Z, consistently shaped for a TIMESTAMP cast; renamed to scheduled_hour_timestamp since it represents the scheduled date and hour as a UTC instant per operator context.
is_airbyte_metadata is true for _airbyte_raw_id, a capture-tool identifier with no business meaning, so it is dropped.
is_airbyte_metadata is true for _airbyte_extracted_at, a capture-tool timestamp, so it is dropped.
is_airbyte_metadata is true for _airbyte_meta, which has a single distinct_value of {} across all rows, so it is dropped as a capture-tool artifact.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across 166158 rows, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is required.

Each row represents one scheduled flight operation; year, month, day, carrier_code, and flight_number are each 0% null and together plausibly identify one flight record, matching the nycflights13 convention of a carrier-assigned flight number per day.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning, so all three are dropped.

Operator convention favors a single DATE column, but each proposal entry maps one bronze column to one target with a unique target_name, so year, month, and day cannot be merged here; they are retained as separate INTEGER columns and a downstream view should compose make_date(year, month, day).
departure_time (dep_time) has null_rate 0.029388 (4883 nulls); per operator context a flight that never departed has no departure time, so nulls are retained rather than imputed.
arrival_time (arr_time) has null_rate 0.0307 (5101 nulls), consistent with flights lacking a recorded arrival; nulls are retained.

departure_delay_minutes and arrival_delay_minutes share the null pattern of their respective time columns (null_rate 0.029388 and 0.032981), so both are retained nullable rather than imputed with zero.
air_time_minutes has null_rate 0.032981 (5480 nulls), aligning with flights missing recorded arrival data; retained nullable.
tail_number (tailnum) has null_rate 0.009154 (1521 nulls) with no stated cause in the profile, so it is retained nullable rather than guessed.

A boolean is_cancelled flag is derived from departure_time being null, since the operator context states a flight that never departed has no departure time, giving reviewers a direct cancellation indicator without dropping rows.

purpose: This table holds cleaned January-June 2013 flight departure and arrival records from JFK, LGA, and EWR as reported to the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, feeding downstream delay, on-time-performance, and route analyses.
usage: Read one row as one scheduled flight operation keyed by year, month, day, carrier_code, and flight_number; consumers should filter or segment on is_cancelled before computing average delays, since departure_time, arrival_time, departure_delay_minutes, arrival_delay_minutes, and air_time_minutes are null for flights that never departed or lack a recorded arrival, and should compose year, month, and day into a date in their own query since this table keeps them as separate integer columns.
limitations: Year, month, and day remain three separate INTEGER columns rather than one DATE column because this cleanup's column actions are one-to-one with bronze columns; dep_time, arr_time, dep_delay, arr_delay, and air_time retain nontrivial null rates (roughly 2.9% to 3.3%) that reflect cancelled or unreported flights and were not imputed; tail_number retains a 0.9% null rate with no documented cause; and the duplicate check only found zero exact-duplicate rows (duplicate_row_rate 0.0), so near-duplicate or clock-drift conditions beyond exact row equality were not evaluated.
